To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the attenuation of the emission intensity of a thin layer can be quantitatively used to determine the layer thickness, and that the attenuation can be used to monitor the local layer thickness in spatially resolved measurements.

(i) the attenuation of soft X-ray emission lines by overlayer materials can be used to determine the layer thicknesses, and that (ii) the attenuation of the emission intensity depends on the energy and the net emission intensity, but (iii) the attenuation of integral emission intensities over large areas is independent of the net emission intensity.
the S L(3) intensity is a function of the ZnO over layer thickness and that the S L emission intensity can be used for quantitative analysis of thin layer structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantitative analysis of the emission intensities in soft X-ray emission spectra (SXES).
the quantitative analysis of soft X-ray emission intensities.
the quantitative analysis of the emission intensities in soft X-ray emission spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantitative analysis of SX emission intensities is a powerful method for determining the thickness of overlayer structures.
the quantitative assessment of the S L emission intensities can be used to determine the local thickness of ZnO overlayers on Cu(In,Ga)Se(2)-based thin-film solar cells.
SXES has the potential to provide quantitative information on buried interfaces and inhomogeneities in thin film solar cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the attenuation of soft X-rays is a useful tool for determining layer thicknesses and for monitoring lateral variations in layer thicknesses in thin-film systems.
the attenuation of S L(2.3) emission is a very sensitive and quantitative tool to monitor thin overlayer thicknesses of up to about 50 nm.
the attenuation of the emission intensity can be used as a quantitative tool for the determination of layer thicknesses in a wide energy range of the emission spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quantitative SXES is possible in a wide energy range, and that it can provide valuable information on the thickness of overlying layers.
the quantitative analysis of SXE can be used to accurately measure the thickness of thin overlayers and to map lateral inhomogeneites.

the quantitative assessment of emission intensities in the soft X-ray energy range can be used to obtain local information about the layer thickness of thin films with an accuracy of a few nanometres, which is sufficient for most practical applications in thin-film solar-cell research.
